 Run It Up take women’s 3x3 tiara
 Leigh Gases 
 • 
 November 18, 2026
 • 
 3 min read
 img]:mx-auto [&_[data-youtube-video]_iframe]:w-full [&_a]:text-blue-500 [&_iframe]:md:mx-auto">
 After a whole afternoon of 3x3 basketball, Run It Up took the 2026 NMIBF Women’s 3x3 Basketball Tournament tiara after beating 4 Lokos in a close final, 12-10, on Sunday, Nov. 15, at the Gilbert C. Ada Gymnasium. 
 Kaia Travilla, Irish Pagarao, Madeleine Alegre, and Yasmeen Younis went up against Rosie Saralu, Cassandra Camacho, Sylvina Simram, and Brit Gopez in the last 3x3 qualifier leading up to the 2027 Pacific Games. The 3x3 format is whoever scores 21 points first wins—or if 10 minutes are up before that, whoever has the most points wins. 
 Run It Up took an early lead, leading by half, 8-4, behind Pagarao’s speed and Travilla’s and Alegre’s accuracy. However, with less than three minutes on the clock, 4 Lokos gained some momentum, with a hot streak by Simram within the paint. 
 Run It Up controlled the ball better though as time ran out and kept 4 Lokos at bay by just two points, 12-10, as 4 Lokos failed to locate the basket once more. 
 Travilla led Run It Up with five markers, while Alegre dished three, and Pagarao and Younis contributed two each. 4 Lokos’ Simram scored five, Saralu shot three, and Camacho scored two. 
 Third place went to FAB 4 after they beat Heart & Hustle, 13-7, before the finals. 
 Younis said of winning the title, “It was definitely rewarding after a long day.” 
 The players haven’t played basketball since after Super Typhoon Sinlaku and with that, Travilla said, “It was really nice that NMIBF was able to do this women’s tournament, because we don’t have much women so it was nice to come out and play with the girls again, so yeah, it was really fun.” 
 Younis added, “It was definitely good to see the different people who played, and more youth definitely, so it was exciting to see.” 
 They then thanked the tourney’s sponsors including Spicy Thai and Angry Penne, as well as the organizers and officials. 
 This is the last 3x3 tourney in a series of tourneys that included the U18 and men’s divisions. Unity Trade was the men’s winner, while Slim Reaperz took the U18 title. 
 With the tourney as a whole, NMIBF’s Alegre said that it was a great turnout. “It was a great turnout for the boys and men’s, and for the women’s, we’re glad we got four teams. Definitely need to work on getting more girls out, but overall it was good.”
